Yes. Practically anything that can be targeted can be replaced with an image with CSS.

You will need to set a background image, as well as a fixed height and width to match that image.

a[href="/user/Kornykory"]::after {
 content: "";
 display: inline-block;
 height: 12px;
 width: 12px;
 background: url(path-to-image.png);
}

  • The content property is required for the ::after pseudo-element to be rendered, but it can contain nothing, hence the "" value.

  • display must be block or inline-block in order to have a fixed height and width, otherwise the element will collapse to the size of its text content.

If you meant post flairs instead of user flairs the principles are still the same — set a background image and height and width.
